relationships.description: The test case seeds fixture records into, or reads records back from, a persistent table or collection to arrange its scenario or assert the stored effect of the behaviour under test.
relationships.evidence: The implementing test's fixture or assertion code inserts into or queries the named table or collection, for example through SQL, a repository call or a seeding script that the test invokes.

relationships.description: The test case design consults the coverage-scope rule for an input field to find out which partition values it is permitted or obliged to choose.
relationships.evidence: In the coverage model, every partition value the sketch picks for that field appears in the selection rule's include list, or is absent from its exclude list.

relationships.description: The test case reads the concrete datum bound in one of its input selections and submits that value for the corresponding input field when it runs.
relationships.evidence: The parameterized row or argument list of the implementing test function contains exactly the datum recorded in the input selection.

relationships.description: The test case builds the request payload described by an operation's request body and sends it, populated with its chosen input data.
relationships.evidence: The test code constructs a JSON or multipart payload with the media type and fields declared in the OpenAPI requestBody and sends it in the operation's HTTP call.

relationships.description: The test case reads derived records from a database view to confirm that the exercised behaviour produced the expected aggregated or projected data.
relationships.evidence: An assertion in the implementing test selects from the named view, or refreshes the materialized view and then queries it.

relationships.description: The test case design is the owning whole of its input selections, and each selection exists only as one binding within that single test case.
relationships.evidence: The coverage model file nests the input selections under the sketch's entry, and deleting the sketch removes them because no other sketch refers to them.

relationships.description: The design of the test case is restricted by a solution-space constraint, such as a ban on production personal data, a mandated test tool or a jurisdictional limit, which narrows how its data and context can be chosen.
relationships.evidence: The sketch, or the decision record it cites, references the constraint, and the sketch visibly complies with it, for example by using synthetic data or the mandated framework.

relationships.description: The test case can only be designed and run meaningfully under the named execution context, such as a load, security or smoke condition with its fixed environment factors.
relationships.evidence: The sketch's context field holds the context variation's identifier, and the implementing test is tagged for, or placed in, the suite whose environment configuration realizes that context.

relationships.description: The test case's choice for an input field is meaningful only in terms of the equivalence classes that the field's partition defines, so changing the partition invalidates that choice.
relationships.evidence: Each partition value chosen in the sketch's input selections belongs to the referenced input space partition in the coverage model.

relationships.description: The test case's expected result is defined by an outcome category, such as validation error or not-found, which determines the class of result its assertions check for.
relationships.evidence: The sketch's expected-outcome field points to the category, and the implementing test asserts the matching result class, for example HTTP 422 for a validation error.

relationships.description: The test case requires another test case to have run first, or reuses the state that the other case establishes, for example an update case that relies on a create case.
relationships.evidence: A test-framework dependency declaration, such as pytest-dependency or TestNG dependsOnMethods, or a shared fixture produced by the other test links the two implementations.

relationships.description: The test case is the verification artifact whose passing execution provides evidence that a shall-statement's acceptance criterion is met.
relationships.evidence: The implementing test carries the requirement identifier in an annotation, tag or traceability matrix entry, and its assertions mirror the requirement's acceptance criteria.

relationships.description: The test case identifies the coverage requirement it was designed to exercise, which places it within that criterion's combination space.
relationships.evidence: The sketch entry in the coverage model has a coverageRequirement field holding the requirement's identifier.

relationships.description: The test case points to the logging pipeline configuration whose exporters and minimum severity it relies on to capture log records for diagnosis or log-based assertions.
relationships.evidence: The test setup loads or overrides the named LoggerProvider or logging root configuration (for example a test logback.xml or an in-memory log exporter) that the sketch cites.

relationships.description: The test case names an instrumented span so that it can correlate its execution with the traced unit of work or assert that the span is emitted.
relationships.evidence: The implementing test uses an in-memory span exporter and looks up, or asserts on, a span with the referenced name and kind.

relationships.description: The test case is anchored to the in-scope production artifact whose behaviour it is designed to exercise.
relationships.evidence: The sketch is nested under, or carries the identifier of, that test coverage target in the coverage model file.

relationships.description: The test case can only run when a specific platform product, such as a database engine, message broker or language runtime, is available in its execution environment.
relationships.evidence: A Testcontainers declaration, docker-compose test service or CI job image in the test setup provisions that engine or runtime at a specific version.

relationships.description: The test case contributes verification evidence toward a stakeholder goal, such as reliable checkout or regulatory confidence, by guarding behaviour that the goal depends on.
relationships.evidence: A traceability matrix or a test-plan document links the sketch, or the suite it belongs to, to the goal identifier.

relationships.description: The test case activates a user-operable control and checks that it starts the expected operation, navigation or state change.
relationships.evidence: A UI test (Playwright, Cypress or Testing Library) clicks or triggers the control through its selector or test id and asserts the resulting effect.

relationships.description: The test case exercises an internal unit of automated behaviour within one component and checks its result for the chosen inputs.
relationships.evidence: A unit or integration test directly invokes the module, class or method that implements the function and asserts on its output or side effects.

relationships.description: The test case reaches the component through a specific access channel, such as a mounted controller, gRPC binding or message listener, to verify that the channel accepts and routes requests correctly.
relationships.evidence: The test drives that channel directly, for example with supertest against the mounted router, a gRPC stub against the server binding or a message published to the listener's queue.

relationships.description: The test case verifies that one of the operations an application service offers to its consumers behaves as specified.
relationships.evidence: The test calls the service's operation through its public facade or client and asserts the returned result or the state change.

relationships.description: The test case runs a business process end to end, from its triggering event to its end state, and checks that the expected business result is produced.
relationships.evidence: A BDD scenario or end-to-end test has steps that mirror the process activities and asserts the final business object or the fulfilled request.

relationships.description: The test case acts as an acceptance check that the business service delivers the expected outcome to its consumer.
relationships.evidence: An acceptance scenario tagged with the business service name asserts the value delivered to the customer, such as a claim being registered or an order being confirmed.

relationships.description: The test case attempts the behaviour that a security control is meant to stop and checks that the control blocks or limits it.
relationships.evidence: A security test tagged with the countermeasure id sends, for example, brute-force or over-limit requests and asserts the rejection, such as HTTP 429 or a lockout.

relationships.description: The test case exercises one combination within the coverage criterion that the requirement defines, and so counts toward that criterion.
relationships.evidence: Coverage-analysis tooling counts the sketch's combination of input, context and outcome toward the requirement's pairwise, boundary-value or MC/DC tally.

relationships.description: The test case verifies a piece of product functionality that a user can perceive, as the persona would use it.
relationships.evidence: An end-to-end or acceptance test is tagged with the feature identifier or ticket, or lives in that feature's test folder, and drives the feature through its user-facing entry point.

relationships.description: The test case mounts a reusable UI component type with a chosen property set and checks its rendered slots and emitted events.
relationships.evidence: A component test or a Storybook interaction test mounts the library component with specific props and asserts its rendered output and its events.

relationships.description: The test case checks that a metric instrument records the expected measurements, with the correct kind, unit and attributes, when the exercised behaviour runs.
relationships.evidence: The test registers an in-memory metric reader and asserts the recorded value for the instrument's name, for example a counter that increments by one.

relationships.description: The test case walks a multi-step user journey from its first step to its final step and checks that the imposed traversal order is enforced.
relationships.evidence: An end-to-end test navigates through the flow's routes in sequence, asserting each step's URL and that skipping a step is prevented.

relationships.description: The test case attempts a navigation under a specific condition and checks that the router guard allows it, or denies it with the expected action.
relationships.evidence: A router test sets the guard condition, for example an unauthenticated state, navigates to the protected route and asserts the redirect or the cancelled navigation.

relationships.description: The test case sends a request to one HTTP method and path pair and verifies that the operation handles its chosen inputs as the contract specifies.
relationships.evidence: The test issues the HTTP call, for example POST /orders, or references the operationId in a contract test, and asserts the status and body.

relationships.description: The test case visits a client-side URL pattern with chosen parameters and checks that the router renders, lazy-loads or forwards to the correct view.
relationships.evidence: The test calls router.push or visits the path (for example /users/42) and asserts that the mapped component is rendered.

relationships.description: The test case checks that a reusable schema definition accepts conforming instances and rejects non-conforming ones for its chosen partition values.
relationships.evidence: The test runs a JSON Schema validator such as ajv against #/definitions/{name} with valid and invalid sample payloads and asserts the outcomes.

relationships.description: The test case simulates the attack technique that a threat-model entry names, in order to check that the system resists it.
relationships.evidence: A security test tagged with the threat id sends the attack payload, for example a SQL injection string, and asserts that it has no effect or is rejected.

relationships.description: The test case attempts a write that violates, or that satisfies, an engine-enforced integrity constraint and checks that the storage engine rejects or accepts it accordingly.
relationships.evidence: An integration test against a real database performs a duplicate, null or orphaned write and asserts an error naming that constraint.

relationships.description: The test case opens a page, screen or dialog and checks that it displays the correct content and behaves correctly for the chosen inputs and context.
relationships.evidence: An end-to-end or component test opens the view through its route or trigger and asserts on its visible elements.

relationships.description: A passing run of the test case is evidence that its share of the coverage requirement's criterion has actually been satisfied.
relationships.evidence: The coverage report marks the requirement's combination as covered by the passing test that the sketch is linked to.

relationships.description: The test case confirms that the actual HTTP response matches the documented response for its status code, including headers and body schema.
relationships.evidence: The test asserts the status code and validates the body against the response schema, for example with jest-openapi toSatisfyApiSpec or a schemathesis check.

relationships.description: The test case confirms that the access-control policy produces the expected permit or deny decision for its chosen subject, resource and action.
relationships.evidence: A policy test, such as an OPA test or an XACML test request, or an authorization integration test, asserts the decision for that policy's target.

relationships.description: A passing run of the test case contributes evidence that the in-scope production artifact behaves as required.
relationships.evidence: Test-run results for the linked test are attributed to the target in the coverage model's verification report.

notes: tests, validates and references to CoverageRequirement overlap; keep references plus validates. references and validates TestCoverageTarget also overlap. accesses InputSelection duplicates composes. accesses InputPartitionSelection is a design lookup, better expressed as references. fulfills-requirements mislabels verification as realization; prefer validates. references LogConfiguration and supports-goals are weak links.
